column1: Tab 12 — What Was Missing, and What v3 Adds

Gap analysis of the v2 engine against the product's users (students and professionals, many neurodivergent) and the Figcit/CESNE survey (n = 244). Each gap has an ID used in Tab 0b column Z. The last column counts how many extended scenarios exercise the gap (live formula). Status tells you whether it is built into the rules here, or still needs a decision or clinical sign-off.

column3: No guard to stop reflection becoming rumination.
column4: Reflection and rumination are different processes; repeated self-focused replay in distress is linked to worse mood.
column5: Rumination family (Tab 2) and pattern 40; RF-2 repeat-topic rule.

column3: No guard for people who find meditation distressing.
column4: Systematic-review evidence reports unwanted effects of meditation in a minority of practitioners; eyes-closed and body-focused practice can be hard in shutdown or high sensory load.
column5: MD-2 contraindication guard and pattern 41; body scan is opt-in only.

column3: No rule on faith neutrality or cultural safety.
column4: Suggesting a religious practice a user has not chosen is intrusive and can alienate users; profile data must not drive spiritual content.
column5: MD-3: practices come only from My Practices or the neutral library; profile fields never select content.

column3: No prayer / quiet room or place-of-worship context.

column5: Two new Tab 3b rows plus a public-context filter row.
